title: Animal Physiology (HL) Adventure 2: Immune response — B and T cells
welcome_lead: Today you'll mount an immune response with B cells, T cells and antibodies.
meta_desc: IBDP Biology HL — innate vs adaptive immunity, B cells, T cells, antibodies, vaccines, monoclonals.
final_note: You learned innate immunity (skin, phagocytes) is general, adaptive (B and T cells) is specific, antibodies recognise antigens, and vaccines train immune memory.

concepts.def: CD4⁺; activates B and cytotoxic T cells

walkthroughs.body_html:
Non-specific, immediate:

- Physical: skin, mucus, cilia, low pH stomach.
- Cellular: phagocytes (macrophages, neutrophils) engulf pathogens.
- Inflammation: histamine → vasodilation → redness/swelling.

B cells (humoral): each clone has a unique antibody receptor. Antigen-binding triggers clonal selection → plasma cells secrete antibodies (IgG, IgM, etc.).

T helper cells (CD4⁺) recognise antigens on MHC II of antigen-presenting cells → activate B and cytotoxic T cells.

Cytotoxic T cells (CD8⁺) recognise MHC I on infected cells → kill them.

Memory cells persist for years — 2° response is faster, larger.

Vaccines train memory without disease — smallpox eradicated 1980 (WHO); polio nearly so.

Monoclonal antibodies are made by fusing B cells with myeloma → hybridoma. Used in pregnancy tests (hCG), COVID treatment (regdanvimab), cancer therapy (trastuzumab).
